generated.title: Excessive use of first person "I" throughout the proposal
generated.description: The guidelines state: "Avoid 'one,' 'I,' and 'our.' Use 'we' sparingly, only for the thesis approach." The student uses "I" approximately 20 times in the main body (Abstract, Objective sections, Schedule) and 4 additional times in the AI Transparency Statement. The text should be restructured to use "we" (sparingly, for the thesis approach) or to omit the subject where the actor is clear from context. For example, "I develop a self-service platform" becomes "We develop a self-service platform" or "This thesis develops a self-service platform"; "I reach this objective when…" becomes "This objective is reached when…" or "We reach this objective when…". The Schedule bullets can drop the subject entirely: "I deliver the Keycloak realm" → "Deliver the Keycloak realm" or "We deliver the Keycloak realm."

locations.quote: In this thesis, **I** develop a self-service platform on which every grant carries an expiry date from the moment somebody requests it.
**I** evaluate the platform at the chair on correctness, administrative efort, and extensibility.

Following the object-oriented software engineering method of Bruegge and Dutoit, **I** pursue four objectives:

locations.section: 4.1 Unify Heterogeneous Resources in One Tree
locations.quote: **I** model the resources as a tree whose folders pass maintainership, audit policy, and grants down to leaves bound to target systems

locations.section: 4.1 Unify Heterogeneous Resources in One Tree
locations.quote: **I** implement the keycloak-group, slack-channel, github-team, and webhook connectors, whose credentials administrators confgure at runtime

locations.section: 4.1 Unify Heterogeneous Resources in One Tree
locations.quote: **I** reach this objective when the webhook connector, written after **I** freeze the framework, needs one new class and one registry entry.

locations.section: 4.2 Enforce an Expiry Date on Every Grant
locations.quote: **I** evaluate correctness with an automated scenario that provisions SSH, Slack, and GitHub access from one approval.

locations.section: 4.2 Enforce an Expiry Date on Every Grant
locations.quote: **I** reach this objective when each access disappears after expiry and, in a second run with the workfow engine disabled on purpose, the drift check reports the remaining SSH membership.

locations.section: 4.3 Delegate the Approval of Requests to Maintainers
locations.quote: Keycloak gates its workfow API on a realm-wide administrative role that maintainers must not hold, so **I** split each decision into a review step

locations.section: 4.3 Delegate the Approval of Requests to Maintainers
locations.quote: **I** reach this objective when administrators perform fewer manual actions and requesters wait less than in the current process.

locations.section: 4.4 Automate the Recertifcation of Active Grants
locations.quote: **I** reach this objective when the platform answers, for any grant, who requested it and why, who reviewed and granted it, when it ended, and who confrmed it since.
**I** divide the work into six iterations of four weeks, each ending with a vertically integrated increment that a user can try in the web application
**I** reserve the fnal two weeks, from 18 to 31 March 2027, as bufer for features that slip from earlier iterations.
**I** deliver the Keycloak realm with OpenID Connect login, SSH key self-service, and the resource tree with inherited maintainers.
